extracted.intended_audience: conference organisers, conference participants (authors, conveners, reviewers) preparing and publishing conference abstracts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance about preparing, submitting and publishing conference abstracts (including extended abstracts/mini-papers) via the ARPHA Conference Abstracts platform, and the platform's publication/indexing/archiving features that affect how abstracts must be produced and disseminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform purpose and machine‑readable publication formats
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPHA Conference Abstracts is an open access, human- and machine-readable platform designed to assist conference organisers and participants in authoring, submission, peer review, editorial management, publication and dissemination of conference abstracts in any field of science, published with DOI in semantic HTML, XML and PDF formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts submitted/published on the platform are expected to be output/presented in semantic HTML, XML and PDF and assigned a DOI; the workflow supports the full life cycle from writing through submission, peer review, publication, dissemination and archiving within a single collaborative environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for extended abstracts / 'mini‑papers' and multimedia content
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform allows innovative publication of extended abstracts ("mini-papers") that may, in addition to the narrative, include data, images, videos and other multimedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video recordings of conference talks or graphic files of poster presentations can be uploaded in bulk after the conference and visualized on each abstract page, enabling abstracts to include or link to underlying data and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted publication types
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform publishes Conference Abstracts in the types: 'Conference Abstract: Poster' and 'Conference Abstract: Presentation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should select the appropriate publication type (poster vs presentation) when preparing/submitting their abstract for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection organization and convener management
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference organisers can subdivide abstract collections by symposia, workshops or sections, and these subdivisions are managed and edited by their respective conveners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisers should structure abstract collections into appropriate thematic subdivisions and assign conveners/editors to manage those sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Works on ARPHA Conference Abstracts are published under an open license (example shown: Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors/publishers must accept/openly license abstracts under CC BY (or the collection's stated license), permitting broad reuse with attribution; check collection-level license for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and discoverability expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts published on the platform are indexed in numerous services (examples listed: Altmetric, ASCI, ASOS Indeks, Baidu Scholar, BASE, ChronosHub, CNKI, CrossRef, Dimensions, EBSCOhost, Google Scholar, Lens, Library of Congress, OpenAIRE, OpenAlex, Scite, Semantic Scholar, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing via ARPHA aims to maximize discoverability across many indexes and aggregators; authors/organisers can expect metadata and DOIs to be propagated to these services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving and long‑term preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPHA Conference Abstracts content is archived in preservation repositories (examples listed: CLOCKSS, Zenodo, Portico, Zendy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts published on the platform benefit from long-term preservation/archiving in recognized services; organisers/authors should be aware of these archives for citation and preservation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serial metadata (ISSN) for the collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARPHA Conference Abstracts collection is assigned an online ISSN (2603-3925).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisers/collections will have serial metadata (ISSN) that can be used for cataloguing and library discovery.
